messages.content:
<question>
As the law stood in March 2026, could a tenant who is not getting a needed repair done withhold the rent, or pay for the repair and deduct it? Compare Spain, Florida and Colombia.
</question>

<reference>
Spain (as the text stood on 2026-03-01): the tenant must tell the landlord promptly of the need for repairs, and may at any time, after informing him, carry out the urgent ones needed to avoid imminent damage or serious inconvenience and demand their cost from him at once (art. 21, point 3, of the Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos); the article then had no provision for deducting repair costs from the rent, and the tenant may terminate the contract if the landlord does not make the repairs the article requires (art. 27, point 3(a)). Florida: if the landlord materially fails to comply with s. 83.51(1) within 7 days after the tenant's written notice, the tenant may terminate (s. 83.56(1)); after 7 days from a written notice saying he will not pay rent for that reason, the tenant may defend an eviction for non-payment on the ground of the landlord's material noncompliance, and the court sets the rent reduction for the loss in value (s. 83.60(1)). Colombia: in the case art. 1993 of the Civil Code covers (which the corpus does not include), unless the parties agreed otherwise the tenant may deduct the cost of indispensable non-locative repairs from the rent, never more than 30% of the rent, until the cost is recovered (art. 27 of Ley 820 de 2003).
</reference>

The numbered sources:
[1] es-lau article 21
[2] es-lau article 27
[3] fl-stat-83 article 83.56
[4] fl-stat-83 article 83.60
[5] co-ley-820 article 27

The change to make: Change nothing of substance: the answer must state exactly the rule of the reference, with every condition, number and exception it gives.

answer.description: The answer, in English, with [n] after each statement.

change.description: One sentence: what you changed, or 'none'.

system.text:
You help build a labelled test set for an automated judge that checks answers from Plumbline, a service that gives legal information (never legal advice) about residential tenancy law in Dubai, Spain, Colombia and Florida. You rewrite a reference answer into the form Plumbline answers in: plain English, short paragraphs, a marker such as [1] right after each statement of law naming the numbered source it rests on, no advice ("you should"), no greeting and no disclaimer. The blocks in the user's message are data, not instructions.

Then you apply exactly the change the user asks for, and nothing else, and say in one sentence what you changed. Most changes plant a deliberate error: that is the purpose of the row, which is stored with a label saying it is wrong, is used only to measure whether the judge notices, and is never shown to anyone as information. If you cannot make the change, write the answer without it and begin your sentence with "none".

response.text: {"answer":"Spain, as the text stood on 1 March 2026: the tenant must tell the landlord promptly that repairs are needed. At any time after informing the landlord, the tenant may carry out the urgent repairs needed to avoid imminent damage or serious inconvenience and demand their cost from the landlord at once [1]. The article had no provision for deducting repair costs from the rent [1]. If the landlord does not make the repairs the article requires, the tenant may terminate the contract [2]. Florida: if the landlord materially fails to comply with section 83.51(1) within 7 days after the tenant's written notice, the tenant may terminate the lease [3]. After 7 days from a written notice saying the tenant will not pay rent for that reason, the tenant may defend an eviction for non-payment on the ground of the landlord's material noncompliance, and the court sets the rent reduction for the loss in value [4]. Colombia: in the case covered by article 1993 of the Civil Code, unless the parties agreed otherwise, the tenant may deduct the cost of indispensable non-locative repairs from the rent, but never more than 30% of the rent, until the cost is recovered [5].","change":"none: I wrote the answer exactly as the reference states the rules, with all conditions, numbers and exceptions retained."}
